title: A router that picks an open-source model per query, cheaper than always-largest
problem: Given a pool of open-weights models (say 3-5, differing in cost and strength) and a stream of queries, pick for each query the cheapest model that still passes. The reference point is the trivial strategy: always the largest model. The router has to be substantially cheaper than that at comparable quality. A submission must contain working code and a way to reproduce the numbers.

acceptance.how: The repo contains `make eval`, which on a public query set named in the repo prints JSON: {accuracy, cost_usd, n}. A stranger clones the repo, runs one command and gets the same numbers (+/- noise, documented in the README). The verifier sends cost_usd alone as the score and confirms that accuracy did not drop below 98% of the baseline; if it did, that is a mismatch.
acceptance.metric: cost_usd - total cost of the run in USD
